4.(1) Unless such member vacates the office earlier under
subsection (2), every member of the Commission shall hold
office for a period from the date of appointment, up to the end
of the term of the Commission.
(2) The office of a member shall become vacant -
(a) upon the death of such member;
(b)  upon  such  member  resigning  from  such  office
by writing addressed   to  the President;
(c) upon such member being removed from office on
any ground specified in subsection (2); or
(d) on the expiration of the term of the Commission
and the consequent expiration of a member’s term
of office.
(3)  A  member  of  the  Commission  may  be  removed
from  office,  by  the  President  with  the  concurrence  of  the
Constitutional Council, if such person –
(a) is or becomes a member of Parliament, or a member
of any Provincial Council or any Local Authority;
(b) is adjudged an insolvent by a court of competent
jurisdiction;
(c) is found by the President, acting on the advice of
the Prime Minister   to have a conflict of interest
with his duties as a member of the  Commission:
Provided  that,  the  Prime  Minister  shall
advise  the  President  in  consultation  with  the
Speaker and the Leader of the Opposition;
(d) is certified on the basis of professional opinion to
be unfit to continue in office by reason of infirmity
of mind or body;
